answers.explanation: Keeping several jobs in memory means the CPU always has one to run.
Interactive computing, with response times under a second.
Swapping moves whole processes; virtual memory needs only part of one in memory.
Privileged instructions only work in kernel mode.
The OS sets the timer before running the program, and the interrupt always comes.
The trap sets kernel mode (0); the return sets user mode (1).
Only a subset of the total jobs is kept in memory.
Increasingly, CPUs support multi-mode operation, like VMM mode for guest VMs.
Processes get a whole chapter of their own later in the course.
